title: A cross-cultural dataset on the structure of social networks: The ENDOW project
abstract: arXiv:2610.28793v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We present multilayer social network data from 50 communities, located in 29 countries around the world, gathered as part of the "ENDOW" project. The communities show exceptional diversity, from fishers in Bangladesh and Vanuatu, to horticulturalists in Fiji and Bolivia, to pastoralists in Namibia and Argentina, to farmers and wage labourers in India and Colombia. Data collection embraced this variation, while still aiming for comparability. Respondents answered ten network prompts on behalf of their "sharing unit" (household), covering different types of material and immaterial support. From these, we construct networks representing flows of support between sharing units in each community. We compare nomination patterns and network summary statistics across the ENDOW communities and to other benchmark datasets. translated_title: 社会网络结构的跨文化数据集：ENDOW项目
translated_abstract: 我们展示了来自全球29个国家50个社区的多层社会网络数据，这些数据作为“ENDOW”项目的一部分收集而成。这些社区展现出极高的多样性：包括孟加拉国和瓦努阿图的渔民、斐济和玻利维亚的园艺种植者、纳米比亚和阿根廷的牧民，以及印度和哥伦比亚的农民与工薪劳动者。数据收集工作在接纳这种多样性的同时，仍力求保持可比性。受访者代表其“分享单位”（即家庭）回答了十个网络提问，涵盖不同类型的物质和非物质支持。基于此，我们构建了刻画每个社区中各分享单位之间支持流动的网络。我们将ENDOW各社区之间的提名模式和网络汇总统计量与其他基准数据集进行了比较。这些汇总统计量表现出相当大的异质性，表明有必要重新审视现有的关于社会网络的“经验法则”。
tldr: 该论文发布了ENDOW项目收集的覆盖29个国家50个多元社区的社会网络数据集，通过家庭间物质与非物质支持流动的网络构建与比较，揭示了社会网络结构的显著异质性，表明需要重新审视既有的社会网络“经验法则”。
en_tdlr: The ENDOW project presents a multilayer social network dataset spanning 50 highly diverse communities across 29 countries, built from household-level flows of material and immaterial support, and reveals considerable heterogeneity in network structure that challenges existing rules of thumb about social networks.
